request.explanation:
Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean normed field with $12\ne 0$ and $\lvert 2\rvert=1$, and let $q\in K^\times$ satisfy $\lvert q\rvert<1$. The Tate series induce a group isomorphism
$$
K^\times/q^{\mathbb Z}\simeq E_q(K).
$$
For a unit outside $q^{\mathbb Z}$, the two affine coordinates of its image are the Tate series $X(u)$ and $Y(u)$.

The point-equation theorem shows that the two series give an affine point away from the powers of $q$. The discriminant makes each such point nonsingular, and the point map sends the powers of $q$ to infinity. The additivity theorem makes this a group homomorphism, and the surjectivity theorem shows that it reaches every curve point.

The kernel is exactly $q^{\mathbb Z}$ by inspection of the point map. Taking the quotient gives the isomorphism. The quotient homomorphism maps the class of a unit to its original Tate point, so the two coordinate identities follow from the affine branch of the point-map definition.
